questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that the stay was outside Europe for exploring new cultures. Singapore being an English-speaking country was also important. As was it important that the university itself was highly acknowledged worldwide.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great stay. I met inspiring people that I today consider some of my best friends. I made a ton of new insides into the world. And I had some of my wildest travel experiences yet.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy. Everything will get send in mails in English and there will be plenty of time and second-chances given if you screw up the initial bureaucratic process. Also, they are very quick at responding to your emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many different options. I can only speak highly of living in a hall.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had to opt for a meal plan. This plan included different options, but most for meat eaters.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is an internal bus-system, which makes transportation easy. Therefore it doesn't really matter if your stay is central on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My specifik room was not good. Was more like a prison cell without airconditioning in 30 degrees heat.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We could switch courses after a few weeks of tryouts. This is especially nice if you want to design your schedule further.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When we applied for NUS we also chose initial courses. When semester started we had some time to switch/drop courses and even more time to switch tutorials. Courses can't overlap. Makes sure they don't. Otherwise you won't get the courses approved.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An online tool. However, if you wanted additional assistance you could text the superviser and get really good help to match the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful. I got pretty much what I wanted and when I wanted it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Perhaps registor for more courses than you want. You can easily drop in the beginning. And most of the courses are very dependent on the lector - some are old and boring. This way you have more options to choose from, when you finally want to settle on courses for the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No. We could only choose a few amounts of courses offered to exchange students. Most of these courses were unambitious and had too little math.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was only allowed to take Level 3000 courses. These are considered BA-level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Tutorials are different from holdundervisning. Tutorials are mainly for testing the students. Not furthering understanding. Also the grading is often spread out over the semester, so that the finals only count for about 40 %. This differs a lot though. Some courses don't even have finals. Most courses have obligatory attendens.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Money and Banking
Evolution of economic though and analysis
ASEAN Economics
Introduction to Game Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take the game theory course. It is closely related to the one at KU.

questions.answer: Getting a new passport.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is cheap. Alcohol is expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good social life on campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine. Not beachvolleyball however...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The swimming hall, but go find out on your own! Try a lot.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Malaysia. The jungle. Explore a lot.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Feel out the system of surveillance, but since everyone speaks English, then the culture shock is not that big.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do stuff before semesterstart. Live in a hall. Live on campus in general.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No, not really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: No criminality. You will feel very safe in Singapore. You can leave your computer or wallet wherever for however long. Nothing will be stolen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Travel, but make sure you have a nice living in Singapore.
Try food.
Go clubbing at Ce La Vi.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, you gotta find out on your own. Everything will work out on its own.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new things I know and have seen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't know. I didn't have any great challenges. I felt alone a few times. Being far away from home can be hard sometimes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Singapore is a great place, because nature and amazing cultures are nearby. Singapore itself is also interesting to explore and understand. A very different country from anywhere in the world and especially Europe.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
